facts.text: Halliday, North Dakota, was founded in 1914, when settlers moved from a site two miles north to establish the town.
The railroad that ran through Halliday became the engine of settlement, but its abandonment in 1984 left the town searching for new growth.
Halliday prides itself on small‑town values, guided growth, and preservation of its historical, cultural, and natural heritage.
The city maintains a wholesome lifestyle rich in cultural history while committing to environmental preservation and a progressive local business approach.
The first post office in Halliday opened in 1900 on William Halliday’s property, giving the town its name.
Halliday’s early settlers were overseas transplants eager to build a new life on the North Dakota prairie.
